office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican Rep. Ed Orcutt of Kalama, in the House since 2002 and ranking Republican on the Finance Committee, faces Democrat Evan Jones, a Port of Longview commissioner and IBEW journeyman who says he ran over Orcutt's vote against a 2025 contractor child-labor bill. Both say the state does not need new taxes; they differ most on tenure and worker-safety enforcement.

candidates.summary: Consulting forester and 12-term state representative who leads House Republicans on tax policy, running on protecting taxpayers, natural-resource jobs and living within existing revenue.
highlights: Voted no on the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and offered three amendments to it, including sending it to voters [S5][S6][S7]
Prime sponsor of bills to repeal the 2025 tax increases and cut the state sales tax [S11]
Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget; says government must live within existing revenue [S10][S3]
Voted no on the 2025 contractor child-labor bill, rent-increase limits and both parents'-rights amendment bills [S23][S12][S13][S14]

taxes.basis: No votes on ESSB 6346 and ESSB 5814, sponsored repeal and tax-cut bills, and repeated statements that he works to prevent tax increases.

spending.basis: Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget and repeatedly says the state is overspending and must live within existing revenue.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 rent-increase limits (EHB 1217); no housing statements.

climate.basis: Voted against the 2025 clean-fuels program changes (2SHB 1409); no climate statements.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296 and ESSB 5181, which amended the parents' rights law; no campaign statement on the topic.

experience.basis: In the House since 2002, Finance Committee ranking member and JLARC vice chair.

candidates.summary: Port of Longview commissioner, IBEW journeyman and Army combat veteran in his first legislative race, running on permitting reform, family-wage jobs and contractor safety.
highlights: Cast the lone port vote against a contractor with a record of safety incidents and wants to close the loopholes that allowed the award [S3][S2]
Says permitting gridlock drives timber, shipping and construction jobs out of state [S1][S2]
Platform plank: 'More Taxpayers, Not More Taxes' [S2]
Pledges to defend the Second Amendment [S2][S3]

taxes.basis: Platform says 'We don't need to raise taxes' and proposes growing the tax base instead; no record.

experience.basis: Port commissioner since 2024 with regional board roles, in his first legislative race against a 25-year incumbent.
